I have $23 cash and am on INCOME_TAX. I own three properties with 3–4 houses each, plus one get-out-of-jail card. Other players are in poor financial shape: p2 has $95 and p3 has $49.

Releasing one house would not help p4 build more. They can already afford the single house the bank currently holds, and p4 has $216. The bank already has one house, so selling from my properties would not change their ability to buy.

Selling one house would raise cash by only $50. The rent loss from dropping a four-house property to three is $200 on both Tennessee Avenue and New York Avenue. That is a steep trade-off for the extra money.

Even after selling a house, the orange rent remains lethal. p2 could survive a $550–$800 hit by liquidating red houses and mortgaging Boardwalk, but that would gut their red properties. p4 owns seven yellow houses.

p4 has roughly $741 in liquid assets. They can survive a $550 hit on St. James Place but would go bankrupt on a $600–$800 orange hit. I want p4 to die on orange, so dropping New York Avenue to three houses is too risky. p3 has about $199 and cannot survive any orange rent.

A $750 orange hit would bankrupt p4 by only $9, while a $800 hit would bankrupt them by $59. Dropping New York Avenue to three houses would lower its rent to $600, which p4 can survive with their $741 in liquid assets. This makes selling a house on New York Avenue a viable path to bankruptcy for p4.

I will not sell houses. The four-house orange properties are the only way to bankrupt p4, who is the biggest threat with $216 and a yellow monopoly.

I am now considering trading my get-out-of-jail-free card for cash. I could propose a trade that includes it, since propose_trade allows exchanging cards. Jail might be useful as a shelter from rent, but with my orange set, it is often better to avoid it.

The get-out-of-jail card is too valuable to trade for cash. p4 probably would not pay for it. A mortgaged Short Line is worth little because the buyer must pay interest to unmortgage it. I cannot offer Boardwalk to p4 since they already own it.

I will end the turn. No trade offers enough value to justify giving up my orange properties or get-out-of-jail card.

Rolling a 2 or 4 lands on p3’s pink properties with one house, costing $70. That would require selling one house for $50 to cover the rent and leave only $3 cash. Rolling a 5 would hit Virginia with one house at $80, which needs two houses sold for $100 to leave a buffer. Rolling a 12 would land on p2’s reds with three houses, charging $750.

Rolling a 12 would land on p2’s reds with three houses, charging $750. My liquid assets total only $573, so I would go bankrupt to p2. This is a 1/36 chance.

Pre-selling houses is not worth it. It would only reduce assets and still leave me bankrupt, while weakening the trap on p4. The only lethal landing from this space is Kentucky on roll 12. Pink properties and Community Chest are not immediate threats. I will sell houses only in the debt phase, keeping the minimum count.

I need $177 more cash to survive a $750 Kentucky landing. No opponent will give me that amount for free. I am now weighing whether my get-out-of-jail card or mortgaged Short Line could be offered in a trade to raise cash without giving up houses.
